hypothesis: The undivided 100 MHz link spends hours clearing routing congestion: the kernel is pinned to SLR1, whose CLBs are 97.7 % used, and routing is 70-80 % of every critical path. The largest single block is the accumulator file -- 131 072 flip-flops and ~42 k LUTs of read multiplexing -- because a reset loop over the whole array stops it being inferred as RAM. Per-lane distributed RAM with a valid bit per (row, lane) standing in for the reset and the row zero computes the same function in a fraction of the area.
evidence_for_hypothesis: u280_nd100 (FP_LAT = 2, 100 MHz) slr_util_placed.rpt: SLR1 CLB 97.71 %, CLB LUTs 70.49 %; rip-up-and-reroute global iteration 0 started at 513 246 overlapping nodes and was still at 2 828 after ~2 h. Hierarchical utilisation of the device (post-synthesis): u_mtx 84 354 LUTs / 139 751 FFs, of which u_acc 41 869 LUTs / 131 072 FFs

microarch.change: storage as VLEN arrays of DEPTH x ELEN, no reset, written per lane (w_en && !z_en && w_lane_en[g]) and read asynchronously; valid[DEPTH][VLEN] flops: reset and z_en clear a row, a write ORs in its lane enables; a lane reads 0 where its valid bit is clear or the row is being zeroed this cycle. Read-old and the zero port's bypass are unchanged, and a zero still drops a same-cycle write
